summary: 为缓解伦敦桥附近的拥堵，布鲁内尔用掘进盾构在泰晤士河底施工，熬过进水、闷热和照明不足等困难。隧道贯通后缺钱修建马车通道，直到接入地下铁路才发挥持续的交通作用。
logic: 港口拥堵催生过河需求
早期掘进失败促成盾构设计
进水与恶劣工况拖慢施工
贯通后无力修马车引道

paragraphs.brief: 伦敦桥成为港口货运瓶颈
sentences: At the beginning of the 19th century, the port of London was the busiest in the world.
19世纪初，伦敦港是世界上最繁忙的港口。

Cargoes that had travelled thousands of miles and survived all the hazards of the sea were unloaded on the banks of the Thames, only for their owners to discover that the most frustrating portion of their journey lay ahead.
货物历经数千英里航程、避过海上种种风险，在泰晤士河岸卸下后，货主才发现最令人头疼的一段还在前面。

Consignments intended for the southern parts of Britain had to be lifted onto horse carts, pulled through the docks and across London Bridge, built in the 12th century and as impractical as its early date implies.
运往英国南部的货物得先装上马车，穿过码头，再挤上建于十二世纪、早已不敷使用的伦敦桥。
By 1820, London Bridge had become the centre of the world’s largest traffic jam.
到1820年，伦敦大桥已成为世界最大交通堵塞的中心。
paragraphs.gist: 十九世纪初伦敦港的海运货物能远渡重洋，却常在最后一程因马车必须经过狭窄拥挤的伦敦桥而陷入堵塞。

paragraphs.brief: 第一次河底隧道尝试失败
sentences: It was an intolerable situation, and it was clear that if private enterprise could build another crossing closer to the docks, there would be good money to be made in tolls paid by users.
这种拥堵令人难以忍受，私人企业若能在码头附近另辟过河通道，使用者愿意付相当高的通行费。
Another bridge was out of the question, as this would deny sailing ships access to the city centre, and ambitious men turned their thoughts to tunnelling beneath the Thames instead.
另建一座桥并不可行，因为它会阻挡帆船驶入市中心，于是一些有雄心的人转而考虑在泰晤士河下挖隧道。
This was not such an obvious idea as it might appear.
这个想法在当时远没有今天看来那么顺理成章。
Although increasing demand for coal had meant a great many tunnels had been dug in mines in Britain, working methods remained primitive.
尽管对煤炭的需求不断增加，这意味着在英国的矿井中挖掘了许多隧道，但工作方法仍然很原始。
Tunnels were dug by men with simple tools, by candlelight.
隧道是由男人用简单的工具，用烛光挖的。
However, in 1807, a group of businessmen got themselves up as the Thames Archway Company.
不过，1807年一批商人还是组建了泰晤士拱道公司。
Their ambition was to tunnel below the Thames, but there was little to guide them as there had been no previous attempt to do this.
他们的目标是在泰晤士河下方挖隧道，但没有什么可以引导他们，因为以前没有试图这样做。
Their chief engineer was Richard Trevithick, designer of the world’s first high-pressure steam engine.
他们的首席工程师是理查德·特雷维希克，世界上第一台高压蒸汽发动机的设计师。
His men made progress at the beginning, but then things began to go disastrously wrong, with muddy soil pouring into the tunnel.
工人起初取得了一些进展，但随后泥浆涌入隧道，工程陷入灾难。
Eventually the Thames Archway Company had had enough.
泰晤士拱道公司最终决定罢手。
Its funds were exhausted, Trevithick was sick from exposure to the river water, and its efforts had proved only that a passage under the river exceeded the limits of contemporary mining technology.
资金已告罄，特里维西克因接触河水而生病；这次尝试只证明当时的采矿技术尚不足以挖通河底。
paragraphs.gist: 另建桥梁会阻挡帆船，商人遂筹资开挖河底隧道，但泥土涌入、资金耗尽，让特里维西克的首次尝试暴露了当时采矿技术的极限。

paragraphs.brief: 钻木生物启发盾构护壁
sentences: At that time, the only machines used in mines were pumps.
当时矿井里使用的机器只有水泵。
It took a man of genius to recognise that a different sort of machine was needed, a machine that could prevent the roof and walls of a tunnel from collapsing.
一位天才工程师看出，还需要另一种机器来防止隧道顶部和两壁坍塌。
This man was Marc Brunel, a Frenchman who had become one of the most prominent engineers in Britain.
这个人是马克・布鲁内尔，法国人，成为英国最著名的工程师之一。
Not long after the failure of the Thames Archway Company, Brunel saw a rotten piece of wood lying on the river bank.
泰晤士拱道公司失败后不久，布鲁内尔在河岸上看见一块朽木。
Examining the wood through a magnifying glass, he observed it was infested with something that looked like a worm.
他用放大镜观察，发现木头里满是虫状生物。
Brunel realised that as it tunnelled through the wood, it would push chewed wood into its mouth and digest it, then excrete a hard substance that lined the new tunnel.
他发现，这种生物钻木时会把啃碎的木屑送入口中消化，又排出坚硬的物质，衬在刚钻成的洞壁上。
Brunel realised that the worm’s digging technique could be adapted to produce a new way of tunnelling.
Brunel意识到，可以对蠕虫的挖掘技术进行改造，以产生新的隧道方式。
His realisation led him to invent a device that has been used in one form or another in most major tunnels built since: the tunnelling shield.
这项观察促使他发明了隧道盾构，此后修建的大多数大型隧道都以某种形式采用了这种装置。
It consisted of a series of iron frames that could be pressed against the tunnel face and supported on a set of horizontal wooden planks that would prevent the face from collapsing.
盾构由一组可推抵隧道开挖面的铁架组成，配合水平木板支护开挖面，防止坍塌。
It was a complex machine and not easy to use, but it seemed that it would protect the miners.
这是一种复杂的机器，不容易使用，但似乎可以保护矿工。
Brunel’s team examined earth samples taken from beneath the riverbed, and subsequently decided to dig the tunnel close to the muddy river bottom, where he could expect to find clay.
团队检测了从河床下提取的土样，决定紧贴泥质河底下方开挖，那里预计能找到黏土。
This would be a more solid and safe substance to dig through than the sand that was found deeper down.
与更深处的沙土相比，黏土更结实，开挖时也更安全。
paragraphs.gist: 布鲁内尔受钻木生物边挖边护壁的方式启发，发明可支撑开挖面的盾构装置，并选取比深处沙层更稳定的河床黏土施工。

paragraphs.brief: 水淹、污浊空气与施工高温
sentences: Brunel began work on his tunnel in 1825, but the problems of such an operation soon became apparent.
布鲁内尔于1825年开始修隧道，但这种行动的问题很快变得很明显。
Although the shield itself worked well, water began to drip into the tunnel.
盾构本身运作良好，然而水开始滴入隧道。

This was more of an annoyance than a danger while the pump was working, but this machine proved unreliable and sometimes failed altogether, meaning that floods began to occur with increasing regularity.
水泵正常时，渗水主要是个麻烦；但水泵并不可靠，有时甚至完全停转，隧道被淹的情况便越来越频繁。
The miners often had to run for their lives.
矿工往往不得不逃命。
Even when Brunel’s men were able to work, they complained of frequent headaches, because the air underground was dirty and contaminated due to the lack of an adequate ventilation system.
即使Brunel的手下能够工作，他们也抱怨经常头痛，因为由于缺乏适当的通风系统，地下空气脏，受到污染。
There were other problems too.
还有其他问题。
Illuminating the tunnels was a constant challenge.
照亮隧道是一个不断的挑战。
Lamps gave off only a weak glow, and there were a number of accidents because the miners could not see what they were doing.
灯光只发出微弱的光芒，而且发生了一些事故，因为矿工看不到他们在做什么。
Lastly, a number of Brunel’s miners walked off the job because they could not tolerate the excessive temperatures that developed in the cramped conditions underground.
还有一些矿工忍受不了狭窄地下空间的酷热，索性辞工不干了。
paragraphs.gist: 盾构能够支撑掌子面，但水泵故障引发水淹，通风差、照明微弱和闷热又使矿工头痛、受伤甚至离开工地。

paragraphs.brief: 隧道贯通却难供马车通行
sentences: Despite all the setbacks, the tunnel finally emerged on the opposite river bank on August 12, 1841.
尽管遇到种种挫折，但隧道终于在1841年8月12日出现在对岸河岸。
Brunel’s triumph, however, was only partial.
但布鲁内尔的胜利只是部分。
The small payment of a penny per person made by the thousands of visitors hardly paid the interest on the government loan he had required to complete the project.
成千上万名参观者每人付一便士，所得几乎连竣工所需政府贷款的利息都付不起。
As a result, there was never enough funding to make it accessible to horse-drawn vehicles, as intended.
因此始终没有足够经费依照原计划改造出入口，让马车通行。
Instead, the passageways were filled with souvenir-sellers by day and the homeless at night, before it was finally closed.
相反，在最后关闭之前，这些通道白天充斥着纪念品销售商，晚上则充满无家可归者。
paragraphs.gist: 隧道虽在 1841 年贯通，参观门票却连贷款利息都难支付，原拟通行马车的设施无力兴建，隧道最终一度关闭。

paragraphs.brief: 旧隧道转为地铁客运线路
sentences: It was only when the underground railway came to London in the 1860s that the Thames Tunnel achieved a measure of real usefulness.
直到十九世纪六十年代伦敦开通地下铁路，泰晤士隧道才真正派上了用场。
It was bought in 1869 by the East London Railway, who found it to be in such excellent condition that it was immediately pressed into service as a route for passenger trains heading east.
1869年东伦敦铁路公司买下隧道，发现其状况极佳，随即用它通行东向客运列车。
The tunnel became, and remains, part of the London Underground network.
隧道成为了并且仍然是伦敦地下网络的一部分
paragraphs.gist: 直到东伦敦铁路公司于 1869 年购入隧道，其良好结构才得以用于客运列车，并延续成为伦敦地铁网络的一部分。

items.en: In the early 19th century, the port of London was considered a safer destination than other ports.
items.zh: 19世纪初，伦敦港口被认为是比其他港口更安全的目的地。
items.why: 文章只提到“海上有风险 (hazards of the sea)”,没有把“伦敦港"与“其他港口做安全性对比，也没有说“伦敦港更安全"。所以 NG。

items.en: London Bridge provided quick access for cargo being sent to southern Britain.
items.zh: 伦敦大桥为货物运往英国南部提供了快速通道。
items.why: 货主发现从泰晤士河把货送往南方十分不便，伦敦桥严重拥堵，无法提供题干所谓快速通道。

items.en: It was generally believed that a new river crossing would be profitable.
items.zh: 人们普遍认为，新建一条过河通道有利可图。
items.why: 文中说靠近码头再建一处过河通道，向使用者收通行费可以赚大钱，正对应预期有利可图。

items.en: Building a second bridge crossing was initially considered to be the best solution.
items.zh: 人们起初认为，再建一座桥是增设过河通道的最佳办法。
items.why: 原文明确说“桥不可能/不考虑 (out of the question)”,题干说“最佳方案”,与原文冲突，所以 FALSE。

items.en: It was believed that coal could be found under the River Thames.
items.zh: 据信，在泰晤士河下可以找到煤。
items.why: 这里说的是“英国矿井里挖隧道与煤需求有关”,不是“泰晤士河下有煤”。原文没有“河下有煤” 的信息，所以 NG。

items.en: The Thames Archway Company were the first group to try tunnelling below the Thames.
items.zh: 泰晤士拱道公司是第一个试图在泰晤士河底挖掘隧道的团体。
items.why: “no previous attempt” = 他们就是第一批尝试者。TRUE。

items.en: Some of Trevithick’s men were injured during a mudslide at his tunnel.
items.zh: Trevithick的一些人在隧道的泥石流中受伤。
items.why: 只说“泥浆涌入”,没说“有人受伤”。受伤信息缺失 = NG。

items.en: The Thames Archway Company ran out of money to finance the tunnel project.
items.zh: 泰晤士拱道公司用尽了隧道工程的资金。
items.why: 公司的资金已经耗尽，直接对应没有钱继续资助隧道工程。

items.en: Preparing to build the tunnel Brunel noticed how a kind of ________ made its tunnels in wood.
items.zh: 筹备修建隧道时，布鲁内尔留意到一种________在木头里钻出通道的方式。
items.why: 回到对应内容“他用放大镜观察，发现木头里满是虫状生物”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Brunel planned to build a shallow tunnel so the earth would have a higher content of ________
items.zh: 布鲁内尔打算把隧道修得浅些，因为较浅的土层中________的含量更高。
items.why: 回到对应内容“团队检测了从河床下提取的土样，决定紧贴泥质河底下方开挖，那里预计能找到黏土”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The miners suffered from ________ because of pollution in the tunnels.
items.zh: 隧道内的污染使矿工饱受________之苦。
items.why: 回到对应内容“即使Brunel的手下能够工作，他们也抱怨经常头痛，因为由于缺乏适当的通风系统，地下空气脏，受到污染”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Lighting problems led to several ________ Some workers quit because of the high temperatures in the tunnel.
items.zh: 照明不良导致了好几起________。隧道内的高温还让一些工人辞了工。
items.why: 回到对应内容“灯光只发出微弱的光芒，而且发生了一些事故，因为矿工看不到他们在做什么”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Brunel did not have enough money to repay his debt to the ________.
items.zh: 布鲁内尔没有足够的钱来偿还欠________的债务。
items.why: 回到对应内容“成千上万名参观者每人付一便士，所得几乎连竣工所需政府贷款的利息都付不起”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 遭受某种不适，在这里指抱怨经常头痛
第 5 段 · 第 4 句
points: 这里说的是“英国矿井里挖隧道与煤需求有关”,不是“泰晤士河下有煤”。原文没有“河下有煤” 的信息，所以 NG。
回到对应内容“成千上万名参观者每人付一便士，所得几乎连竣工所需政府贷款的利息都付不起”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Cargoes … were unloaded on the banks of the Thames, only for their owners to discover that the most frustrating portion of their journey lay ahead.
“that had travelled thousands of miles and survived all the hazards of the sea”修饰前面的 Cargoes。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 Cargoes，再把修饰信息接回主句。
连接词 although 引出“Although increasing demand for coal had meant a great many tunnels had been dug in mines in Britain”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: The first tunnel ever to be built under a major river was the tunnel under London’s River Thames
伦敦泰晤士河下的隧道是第一个在主要河流下建造的隧道
